data.content_ref: inline:The target's defense collapses when applied to Popper's own requirement for 'acting' on a theory. The claim that preference is merely acknowledging a theory 'hasn't been proven false yet' fails to explain why one should act on Theory A (survived) over Theory B (untested or less tested) if survival confers no positive status or probability. If the elimination of rivals does not logically increase the standing of the survivor, then preferring the survivor for practical action is indistinguishable from an inductive bet that the future will resemble the past (i.e., that what worked before will work again). The target asserts this is not an inductive leap, but offers no non-inductive mechanism to bridge the gap between 'not yet falsified' and 'rationally preferred for action,' thereby smuggling in the very justificationist assumption it claims to reject.
